lifecycles._note: FileStorage SNAPSHOT + SNAPSHOT-SCHEDULE + REPLICATION lifecycle (billable NFS volume -> heavy, gated by SCP_RUN_HEAVY). LIVE VALIDATED 2026-06-24 covering 17/21 endpoints. Flow: create NFS volume (202) -> snapshot (202) -> restore snapshot (202) -> set-volume (202) -> snapshot-schedule create (202) + list (200) + set (202) + delete (202) -> replication create (202) + list (200) + show (200) + set (400 product-constraint) + delete (400 product-constraint) -> delete snapshot (202) -> delete volume (blocked if replication exists). KEY FINDINGS: (1) Volume create: {name, protocol:NFS, type_name:HDD} -> 202. Response has $.volume_id (flat). Volume name auto-appended with suffix (regrfsr001 -> regrfsr001_fwfufh). (2) Volume immediately available (state:available right after create, no poll needed for create-snapshot). (3) snapshot create: {volume_id} -> 202, $.snapshot.id. (4) snapshot restore: PUT /v1/snapshots/{id}/restore?volume_id=... with body {} -> 202. (5) snapshot-schedule create: {volume_id, snapshot_retention_count, snapshot_schedule:{frequency, day_of_week, hour}} -> 202. No id in create response; get id from list response $.snapshot_schedule[0].id. (6) replication create: {name, volume_id, region:kr-east1, replication_frequency:5min, replication_type:replication, backup_retention_count:2} -> 202. Captures $.replication_id. (7) PRODUCT CONSTRAINT: setvolumereplication AND deletevolumereplication BOTH return 400 filestorage.BadRequest.Invalid.volume.purpose when volume.purpose=original (source of active replication). Cannot be done from source side — requires DR region access or console. (8) PRODUCT CONSTRAINT: deletevolume returns 400 'cannot delete volume because replication is in use' while replication exists. Teardown sequence: first set policy to paused, then delete replication, then delete volume — BUT set-policy also fails with volume.purpose. RESOURCE LEAK: each run creates stranded volumes+replications requiring console cleanup. (9) setaccessrule: SCALAR body {object_id, object_type, action}. Returns 404 NotFound for fake VM uuid — needs real VM id (needs-peer blocker).

steps.name: set-volume
steps._note: Closes setvolume (PUT /v1/volumes/{volume_id}) — no other lifecycle covers it. Body VolumeSetRequest: {file_unit_recovery_enabled: bool}.

steps.name: set-access-rule
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: setaccessrule uses SCALAR body (not array): {object_id, object_type, action}. Returns 404 VirtualServer.VirtualServerNotFound for fake UUID — the VM validation runs. PRODUCT CONSTRAINT / NEEDS-PEER: requires a REAL VM id. No VMs in account. Steps is optional+tolerant to reach the endpoint (records as 404 soft). object_type enum: VM|BM|GPU|GPU_NODE|ENDPOINT. action enum: add|remove.

steps.name: list-snapshot-schedules
steps._note: Closes listsnapshotschedule (GET /v1/snapshot-schedules) — probe_reads skips it (no path params, only the required ?volume_id= query). volume_id is a REQUIRED query param (live 400 without it). PROVEN 200 with a real volume_id. capture_soft fallback: grabs snapshot_schedule_id from the list response ($.snapshot_schedule[0].id) in case the create response did not carry it — needed by set-snapshot-schedule and delete-snapshot-schedule steps.

steps.name: create-replication
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: createvolumereplication returns 202 with real volume_id. Response has $.replication_id and $.replication_volume_id (the DR volume in kr-east1). TEARDOWN: Once created, volume.purpose='original'. The DR side (kr-east1) must be used for set/delete. Teardown sequence: use SCP_REGION=kr-east1 or SCP_SERVICE_HOSTS to set policy=paused via $.replication_volume_id, then delete replication, then delete volume. The set-replication-dr and delete-replication-dr steps below use the 'filestorage-dr' service alias -- set SCP_SERVICE_HOSTS='{"filestorage-dr":"https://filestorage.kr-east1.e.samsungsdscloud.com"}' at runtime to enable cleanup.

steps.name: list-replications
steps._note: Closes listvolumereplications (GET /v1/replications) — probe_reads skips it (no path params, only the required ?volume_id= query). volume_id is a REQUIRED query param (PROVEN 200 with real volume_id). capture_soft fallback: grabs replication_id from the list response ($.replications[0].replication_id) in case the create step 4xx'd (DR region unavailable) — needed by get-replication, set-replication, delete-replication steps.

steps.name: get-replication
steps._note: id-bound read (show replication). Closes the replication_id getid GET /v1/replications/{replication_id}. Keys off the create-replication-captured replication_id; tolerant [200,400,403,404] because replication create targets a remote DR region (kr-east1) and may 4xx (DR/region unavailable), leaving replication_id a placeholder that normalizes to the catalog '*' key. Makes the endpoint statically reachable (complements probe-reads).

steps.name: set-replication
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: setvolumereplication returns 400 filestorage.BadRequest.Invalid.volume.purpose from source side. PRODUCT CONSTRAINT: cannot SET from source. The step reaches the endpoint but gets 400. Valid body: {replication_update_type: 'policy'|'modify_schedule', replication_policy: 'use'|'paused' (for policy type), replication_frequency: '5min'|'hourly'|'daily'|'weekly'|'monthly' (for modify_schedule)}. To achieve 2xx: use 'filestorage-dr' service (DR side) with dr_volume_id as volume_id param — see set-replication-dr step below.

steps.name: set-replication-dr
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: setvolumereplication returns 202 from DR side (kr-east1) using the DR volume_id. Uses 'filestorage-dr' service alias. Set SCP_SERVICE_HOSTS='{"filestorage-dr": "https://filestorage.kr-east1.e.samsungsdscloud.com"}' to enable. Pausing the replication policy is required before deletion (deletevolumereplication also requires paused state). Uses dr_volume_id captured from $.replication_volume_id in create response.

steps.name: delete-replication
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: deletevolumereplication returns 400 filestorage.BadRequest.Invalid.volume.purpose from source side. PRODUCT CONSTRAINT: cannot delete from source. The step reaches the endpoint but gets 400. See delete-replication-dr step for the working teardown path.

steps.name: delete-replication-dr
steps._note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-24: deletevolumereplication returns 202 from DR side (kr-east1) using the DR volume_id. MUST be called after set-replication-dr (policy=paused). Uses 'filestorage-dr' service alias — set SCP_SERVICE_HOSTS='{"filestorage-dr": "https://filestorage.kr-east1.e.samsungsdscloud.com"}' to enable. When enabled, this step enables proper teardown so the source volume (purpose reverts to 'none') can then be deleted.
